chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If a male slave has a female slave under his ownership, and he divorces her, and then his master frees her, she remains with him in the state of one (i.e., she is not freed independently but remains a slave alongside him).

key_terms.عَلَى وَاحِدَةٍ: In one state/status (remaining together as slaves)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a female slave if her master frees her after her husband (also a slave) divorces her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the legal principle that a female slave's emancipation is contingent upon her master's action, not merely her marriage to a freed male slave. It highlights the Shia juristic view that upon the master freeing the male slave and divorcing the female slave, her status remains tied to the male slave's condition until she is explicitly freed by her own master, preserving the structural integrity of the master-slave relationship in inheritance and marriage law.
